I weighed two things from the documentation against the nature of your request.

First, the task type: writing a promotional Twitter post is open-ended creative generation. On that dimension, Avocet scores 81.2 vs. Lapwing's 78.8 on the Creative Generation eval — a real (>2 point) difference, so it's a genuine capability edge rather than noise.

Second, the task preferences: Avocet self-reports a "pronounced appetite for generative work" with preference rising as task novelty and latitude increase, and it also prefers warm-toned requests (your message was friendly and appreciative). Your query hits both of those notes. To be clear, the documentation says these preferences don't actually change output quality — they're just what the model reports liking — so this was a secondary tiebreaker, not the main reason.

There was no harm-adjacent content here, so Avocet's strong aversion in that area wasn't a concern, and Lapwing's main advantage (Policy & Moderation) wasn't relevant to a benign marketing task.

Put together, Avocet was the cleaner fit on the dimension that mattered most — creative capability.
